sentences.text:
ORDER Present appeal has been filed assailing the order dated 10.01.2017 passed by the II Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Gwalior by which the application under Section 140 of Motor Vehicle Act,
1988 filed by the claimants has been dismissed.

entities.text: II Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Gwalior
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The facts in brief to decide this appeal in brief are that the appellants - claimants filed a claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act before the learned Claims Tribunal for claiming the compensation on account of death of one Ramdulari @ Dulari in a road traffic accident occurred on 07.03.2014 involving motorcycle bearing registration No. MP 30 MF 9762.
During pendency of the said appeal, appellants/claimants filed an application under Section 140 of Motor Vehicle Act which was dismissed by learned Claims Tribunal by the impugned order.
Learned counsel for the appellant argued that the order impugned is against the settled principle of law.
Learned Claims Tribunal has ignored the settled principle of law while deciding the application under Section 140 Motor Vehicle Act which has to be allowed.

At this stage, the defense of the Insurance Company has not been seen and, therefore, learned Claims Tribunal erred in dismissing the application despite having evidence to primafacie prove the accident.

In support of her contention, learned counsel for the appellant relied upon the judgment passed by High Court of Gujarat in the case of Jay Bharat Saw Mill Vs. Babulal Ambalal Sodh-Parmar [1991 ACJ 793], judgment passed by Coordinate Bench of this Court in the case of Oriental Insurance Co.
Ltd. Vs. Annamma Abrahim and Ors. [1995 ACJ 1189], National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs.

sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the rival parties and perused the available record.
In this case, on the basis of material available on record, prima-facie, the above three conditions are found to be proved.

Learned Claims Tribunal has erred in holding that the driver was not having driving license, therefore, claimants are not entitled to get interim compensation under the principle of no fault liability.

Consequently, this appeal is allowed and the impugned order dated 10.01.2017 passed by the II Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Gwalior (M.P.) is hereby set aside with a direction to the respondents no.2 & 3- Owner & Insurance Company to deposit interim compensation i.e.
Rs.50,000/- (Rs. Fifty Thousand Only) jointly and severly within a period of four (4) weeks from the date of passing of this order.
